claude.sample_unit: LLM responses (25 hypothetical cases x 4 panels)

links.outcome: Quality scores of LLMs with versus without guideline document integration
links.effect: Base ChatGPT 4.5 scored 22.76/25 vs 21.42 for guideline-loaded ChatGPT 4.5 and 21.56 for NotebookLM + guideline; base model significantly superior to three panels; differences in accuracy (p=0.0006) and guideline compliance (p<0.0001).
links.quote: the lack of benefit from guideline uploading suggests unstructured presentation may be inadequate for integration.

links.outcome: Expert-rated guideline adherence and contraindication awareness of LLM osteoporosis recommendations
links.effect: Panels differed in scientific accuracy (p=0.0006) and guideline compliance (p<0.0001); safety/contraindications awareness was the lowest-rated criterion in base models.
links.quote: Safety/contraindications awareness was lowest-rated criterion in base models.

links.outcome: Hallucination rate in LLM responses assessed by geriatricians
links.effect: Hallucinations were detected in one Gemini 3 base-model case (4%).
links.quote: Hallucinations were detected in one Gemini 3 base-model case (4%).

openai.sample_unit: LLM responses to hypothetical osteoporosis cases

links.effect: Base ChatGPT 4.5 scored 22.76/25 vs guideline-loaded ChatGPT 4.5 21.42 and NotebookLM+guideline 21.56; Friedman χ²=18.377; p=0.0004.
links.quote: The ChatGPT 4.5 base model achieved the highest quality score (22.76/25; 95% CI: 22.30–23.22), followed by Gemini 3 (21.80), NotebookLM + guideline (21.56), and ChatGPT 4.5 + guideline (21.42).

links.effect: Scores differed across panels (Friedman χ²=18.377; p=0.0004); ChatGPT 4.5 base was significantly superior to three panels.
links.quote: Bonferroni-corrected comparisons showed ChatGPT 4.5 base model was significantly superior to three panels.

links.effect: Safety/contraindications awareness was lowest-rated criterion in base models.
